title: two module-local Error classes sharing a durable failure identity are refused before an executable artifact can be published

xfail.reason: Both native profiles now report VIBE1150@15:32, including namespaced Error declarations in the source module's nominal identity space. Their remaining difference is contract-validation stage: executable-body Manifest derivation adds VIBE4199@19:29, while standalone Plan emission adds VIBE4124@20:10 naming both Failed classes and their colliding durable identity. Both refuse and publish no executable artifact; the previous nominal-classification disagreement is retired. Measured 2026-09-07.
xfail.doc: specification/durable-execution.mdx §Durable Boundary Contract; specification/failures.mdx, Error Classes. The same source-module nominal claim is refused on both profiles.

notes: specification/durable-execution.mdx §Durable Boundary Contract requires an unambiguous durable failure identity: replay cannot choose between two constructors under one recorded identity. Distinct class names and distinct source modules have separate positive controls. Here both declarations really are named Failed in one source module, under different namespaces. Native source analysis refuses the second nominal claim with VIBE1150, and executable-body Manifest derivation refuses the underivable Action contract with VIBE4199 before publishing any artifact. Both diagnostics and their substantive messages are required. The 2026-09-07 native-only migration removes the retired frontend's omission of the nominal error. This case no longer declares VIBE4124 as the SDK observation: that precise Action-call diagnostic remains observable in standalone Plan emission, recorded by the existing comparison marker. The current code census must not count it as a declared-code probe.
